content.definition: Hybrid coronary revascularization (HCR) is defined as combined or consecutive procedures consisting of an internal mammary artery graft to the left anterior descending artery (LAD) and PCI to the other non-LAD vessels for the treatment of multivessel disease (MVD).
content.preferred_surgical_technique: Minimally invasive left anterior mini-thoracotomy or robotic-assisted left internal mammary artery (LIMA)-LAD.
content.rationale: Combine prognostic benefits of a LIMA graft to the LAD with benefits of contemporary PCI with DES for disease in arteries that otherwise would be revascularized using vein grafts (which are prone to occlusion).
content.evidence_and_decision_making: Limited evidence from RCTs to support hybrid revascularization. Clinical decision-making should involve the Heart Team.
clinical_criteria_supporting_HCR: ACS patients with an indication for CABG may include MVD with LAD suitable for CABG and non-LAD lesions suitable for PCI
Unprotected left main coronary artery that is unsuitable for PCI
content.recommendation_table_reference: Recommendation Table 12 (link: Open in new tab)

recommendation_summary.general: Base revascularization strategy (IRA PCI, multivessel PCI/CABG) on the patient's clinical status and comorbidities and disease complexity according to principles of myocardial revascularization.
recommendation_summary.class_level: Class I, Level B for individualized strategy

cardiogenic_shock.IRA_only: IRA-only PCI during the index procedure is recommended (Class I, Level B).
cardiogenic_shock.staged_PCI_non_IRA: Staged PCI of non-IRA should be considered (Class IIa, Level C).
